paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people in Newham, including the council's own fostering service and independent agencies. The council announced in January 2026 that Ofsted had judged its children's services outstanding in every area, and the inspector noted the excellent support foster carers receive.

Newham needs carers for babies and toddlers, children under 12 and teenagers, and many of its carers look after a teenager long-term until they are ready to live on their own. It also places young parents with their babies, with the carer helping the parent build confidence and skills. Its July 2026 campaign, "Be the missing piece", asked for homes for sibling groups and for children with disabilities or who have lived through complex trauma, and set out to reach more carers from the borough's Bangladeshi and Black African communities. The council says it relies on independent agencies when it needs a home for a child quickly.

The council lists payments of up to £866.53 a week, its specialist carer rate, with a separate allowance for the child on top, plus extra payments for birthdays, holidays and festivals, a £750 setting-up grant for furniture and equipment, full Council Tax exemption, and £1,000 if someone you recommend is approved and takes their first child. Support includes your own social worker, a 24-hour line, a monthly support group, the local foster carers' association, free Fostering Network membership and a place on its Mockingbird programme. Carers approved elsewhere can transfer, and the council aims to complete that assessment in under 12 weeks.

The council holds online information sessions and drop-ins at Stratford and Canning Town libraries. Talk to the council and two or three services above before you choose, and see the Hackney and London pages too.
